study: deriv-ml, addendum (desk instructions received during the run, frozen before any addendum target, model or sequence model was computed)
relation_to_rule: derivml_rule.json and its amendment are unchanged; P1 and P2 stay as frozen. Everything here is secondary, in the same Benjamini-Hochberg family (q = 0.10), reported per group and class: DIFF 1s (VOL1), DIFF 2s (VOL2), DIFF HF, STEP, JUMPY (BC, JUMP), RB; three-part reporting (skill on the null, real minus null = behavioural skill, the after-cost trade with tick fills on BC/JUMP/RB). Day-bootstrap 90% intervals (300 draws).
state_when_frozen: the main rule's datasets were built for DIFF, STEP and RB (JUMPY waits for the Jump ticks) and the main models were running; no addendum quantity had been computed
rows_features_splits: the main datasets' rows, features (the first-frozen set used by the main models), per-series splits, fit / calibration / confirmation masks and nulls (DIFF: iid, garch, gen; STEP, JUMPY, RB: gen). Addendum targets are computed from the same bars of each source (real or null), aligned by series and bar
spike_bars: JUMPY and RB report every addendum target with and without spike bars. A spike bar is a bar whose spike-side excursion (Boom H - O, Crash O - L, Jump and RB max(H - O, O - L)) over ATR_t is at or above the series' discovery 90th percentile (the main rule's J definition, applied to RB too). 'Without' drops the rows whose target window (t+1..t+h) contains a spike bar; 'with' keeps all rows. The models are the same; only the scored rows differ

A_price.targets: c1 = (C_{t+1} - C_t)/ATR_t, h1 = (H_{t+1} - C_t)/ATR_t, l1 = (L_{t+1} - C_t)/ATR_t, ck = (C_{t+k} - C_t)/ATR_t (k of the main rule: 24 / 6 / 5). Models fit the ATR-scaled move; price levels are C_t + ATR_t x prediction
A_price.baselines: naive: c1 = ck = 0; h1 = +m_h, l1 = -m_l with m_h, m_l the series' discovery fit-row means of h1 and -l1 (the last close plus or minus the expected half-range); the null-trained twin (same models trained and scored on the null)
A_price.metrics: R2_OS against naive = 1 - SSE_model / SSE_naive (the headline); R2 on the ATR-scaled moves; level R2 of model and of naive (both near 1, meaningless, shown to say so); RMSE, MAE, MAPE on levels; Theil's U (RMSE_model / RMSE_naive); directional accuracy of c1 and ck; corr(pred, actual); Mincer-Zarnowitz intercept and slope (OLS of actual on prediction); Diebold-Mariano (squared-error differential against naive, day-clustered t and the day-bootstrap one-sided p)
A_price.intervals: CQR at 0.05 / 0.95 on c1 (HGB quantile loss) with split and ACI (gamma 0.005) as the main rule; baseline interval = naive plus the fit-row 5% / 95% residual quantiles, with the same ACI; coverage and mean width

B_volatility_regression_metrics: for rvk, range1, absret1 from the main runs: R2 of log y (log realised variance), R2_OS of each model against HAR and against the generator constant (gen) in log space and QLIKE, Mincer-Zarnowitz on log y, corr. A positive R2_OS over gen on a constant-volatility index (DIFF, STEP) means a bug or a change in the feed

C_returns.targets: lr1, lr3, lr6, lr12 = log(C_{t+k} / C_t) for k in 1, 3, 6, 12 bars; z1 = lr1 / (ATR_t / C_t) (ATR-scaled); oc1 = log(C_{t+1} / O_{t+1}) (the next bar's open-to-close). Models fit the vol-scaled return (r / (ATR_t / C_t)); metrics on raw log returns
C_returns.metrics: R2_OS against zero and against the historical mean (the series' discovery fit-row mean); RMSE; MAE; directional accuracy; IC and rank IC = cross-sectional Pearson / Spearman correlation of prediction and outcome across the group's indices at each bar time (bar times with >= 3 indices), averaged; Mincer-Zarnowitz
C_returns.portfolio: per group and timeframe, for lr1 and the k = 6 return: at each bar time with >= 3 indices, long the top third and short the bottom third by prediction, equal weights, held k bars (overlapping books 1/k each for k > 1), net of the spread (each position change pays half the spread in log terms on each leg) and swap; annualised Sharpe with a day-bootstrap 90% interval; real against the null

D_sequence_models.inputs: per bar, 12 OHLC-derived channels in ATR units of the previous bar: (O-C_{-1}), (H-C_{-1}), (L-C_{-1}), (C-C_{-1}), (H-L), body, upper and lower wick, log(ATR_t / ATR_{t-1}), and the bar's spike-side excursion (JUMPY/RB) or 0; windows 32, 64, 128 bars ending at t
D_sequence_models.architectures: LSTM (1 layer, 32 units) and GRU (1 layer, 32 units), the last hidden state into one linear head per target (multi-task): sign1, signk, tup10, tdn10, z1, zk (k-bar return / ATR), log rvk, log range1, the H = 20 trend sign and slope, the 5-day band up / down, the L = 50 range break up / down (5 days), and spk on JUMPY; losses: BCE for binary heads, MSE for the regression heads (standardised on discovery), summed with equal weights
D_sequence_models.training: discovery fit rows only (the main rule's 80%, purged by the horizon), with early stopping on a discovery-internal validation block (the last 15% of fit rows by time, purged and embargoed by 128 bars + the longest horizon) on the summed loss, patience 3, at most 15 epochs of at most 100,000 sampled windows, Adam lr 1e-3, batch 512, CPU, torch threads 2
D_sequence_models.search: the window (32 / 64 / 128) chosen for the LSTM with seed 0 by the validation loss; then LSTM and GRU at that window with seeds 0, 1, 2; the seed spread (min / max of the metric) reported. The identical procedure runs on every null
D_sequence_models.order: 1d, then 4h, then 1h only if the lab allows (at most 4 workers, shared with the FX study); torch 2.14 CPU is in the lab .venv (nothing installed)
D_sequence_models.scoring: the seed-averaged prediction is scored with the same metrics as the tabular models on every head's target; conformal sets (ACI) for sign1

E_range_breakout.bands: round-number bands: per index a frozen width W = 10^m (m integer, or the index's point size if larger), chosen on discovery as the power of ten whose W / median daily ATR is nearest to 4 (log distance); the band containing C_t is [floor(C_t/W) W, +W). Targets for k = 1, 5, 20 days (1h 24/120/480, 4h 6/30/120, 1d 1/5/20 bars): band_up = a high at or above the band's upper edge within k bars, band_dn = a low below its lower edge, band_first = which comes first (bars touching both, or neither within k, excluded)
E_range_breakout.ranges: the trading range: hiL / loL = the highest high / lowest low of bars t-L+1..t, L in 20, 50, 100. Targets for k = 1 and 5 days: rng_up = a close at or above hiL + 0.5 ATR_t within k bars, rng_dn = a close at or below loL - 0.5 ATR_t, rng_first = which first, rng_ext = after the first break, the largest further excursion beyond the broken level within the rest of the k bars, in ATR_t (regression on broken rows)
E_range_breakout.first_passage_baseline: mandatory: P(hit) given the distance to the level in ATR_t / sqrt(k), horizon and volatility state, learned on the group's generator null (the gen source: tick-rate GBM, the fitted step walk, the fitted compound-jump / jump-diffusion simulators, rbsim), i.e. jumps included: a small HGB (max_leaf_nodes 15, 200 iterations) on [distance up / sqrt(k), distance down / sqrt(k), atr_ratio, lvol_z, class flags] fitted on the null's discovery fit rows; applied unchanged to the real rows and to the null's own confirmation. Skill is only what beats it
E_range_breakout.models: linear (logistic, regression for rng_ext) and HGB (main rule default) on the main features plus the target's distance features
E_range_breakout.round_numbers: do round numbers behave differently on the served feed: the calibration gap mean(y - p_fp) on real minus the same on the null, per group, k and side, day bootstrap
E_range_breakout.metrics: AUC, Brier, Brier skill against the first-passage baseline, reliability, ACI conformal sets (singleton rate and accuracy), behavioural AUC (real minus null) of the model and of model-minus-baseline
E_range_breakout.trade: only if a cell beats the first-passage baseline (BH) on real AND on real-minus-null; then the main rule's trade with the target side, tick fills on BC/JUMP/RB

F_forward_trend.horizons: H in 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 bars at 1h, 4h, 1d; targets use bars t+1..t+H only; purge and embargo by H (labels resolve at t+H)
F_forward_trend.primary_labels: on HLC3 = (H+L+C)/3 of bars t+1..t+H: tr_sgn = sign of the LRC(H) slope; tr_slope = slope / ATR_t (ATR per bar); tr_R = the channel's Pearson R (trend quality); tr_cls = up / range / down by z = slope x (H-1) / (ATR_t sqrt(H)): up if z > 0.5, down if z < -0.5 (frozen); tr_mcfl = the MCFL v2 state (lrc_retest.pivots / structure, 3/3 pivots) known at bar t+H
F_forward_trend.secondary_labels: the same sign from (i) one regression through all four prices O, H, L, C of each bar (OHLC); (ii) HLC3 weighted by tick volume (the bars' tick_volume, real only; the generator nulls have a constant tick count per bar, so the weights are equal and the variant equals HLC3: degenerate by construction there; the real feed's tick-count CV per bar is reported to say whether it is degenerate on real too); (iii) closes only, the contrast
F_forward_trend.baselines: persistence computed the same way: the backward LRC(H) on HLC3 of bars t-H+1..t (sign, slope, R, class) and the MCFL state at t; and the null-trained twin
F_forward_trend.models: linear and HGB (main default) for tr_sgn, tr_slope, tr_R, tr_cls (multiclass), tr_mcfl (multiclass); the secondary labels: tr_sgn only, persistence and HGB
F_forward_trend.metrics: AUC (one-vs-rest macro for 3 classes), Brier, reliability, R2_OS (slope against zero and against persistence), IC (cross-sectional, as C), ACI conformal singleton rate and accuracy for tr_sgn; behavioural skill per group, class, timeframe and H; JUMPY and RB with and without spike bars
F_forward_trend.trade: only if a cell beats both persistence and the null twin (BH): the main rule's trade in the predicted trend direction, P(N R) against the null, tick fills on jump instruments

budget: tabular addendum models per (timeframe, group, source) job: linear on all fit rows, HGB on at most 200,000 fit rows (a fixed random subset, as fxml's ablation budget); walk-forward HGB and the online SGD learner for the A and C targets only
plots: R2_OS by group, model and timeframe, real vs null; IC and the long-short Sharpe; price interval coverage and width; first-passage reliability and calibration gap (round numbers); trend skill vs H per group, real vs null; sequence-model seed spread; with/without spike bars
